Where it began

Mushfiqur Rahim was born in Bogura on 9 May 1987 and went to Bogura Zilla School. He trained at the Bangladesh Institute of Sports and came through the Under-19 side, which he captained at the 2006 Under-19 World Cup in Sri Lanka. Two of his team-mates there were Shakib Al Hasan and Tamim Iqbal, so it was quite a dressing room. They reached the quarter-finals.

He had already been to Lord's by then. Picked for Bangladesh's first tour of England in 2005, he batted his way into the first Test with runs in the warm-up games and, aged 17, made 19 in a total of 108. Somewhere in the middle of all this he also studied history at Jahangirnagar University, finishing a master's degree in 2012.

The player

By November 2026 he had played 107 Tests between 2005 and 2026, making 7,040 runs at 39.11 with 14 hundreds and 30 fifties. Behind the stumps he held 97 catches and made 15 stumpings, and in 2017 he became the first Bangladesh keeper to reach 100 Test dismissals.

The big innings are the ones people recall. At Galle in March 2013 he made the first double hundred by a Bangladeshi in Tests. In November 2018 he batted for 589 minutes to make 219 not out against Zimbabwe, becoming the first wicketkeeper to score two Test doubles, and in February 2020 he added a third, 203 not out, again against Zimbabwe. He led Bangladesh in 34 Tests between 2011 and 2017, and was the first from his country to reach 5,000 and then 6,000 Test runs.

What made him special

Patience and adaptability. On that first tour of England he reworked his method during the warm-up games to cope with the moving ball, and it earned him a Test place. He could switch gears too: in a one-day game against Ireland in 2023 he reached a hundred from just 60 balls, at the time the fastest by a Bangladeshi.

The road was not always smooth. After the 2007 World Cup there was a lean patch in which five innings brought him four runs between them, and he briefly lost his place. He came back as the first-choice keeper, which tells you most of what you need to know.

Away from the middle

He was named in the ICC ODI Team of the Year for 2021, and that May he became the first Bangladeshi to be part of 150 international wins. He played franchise cricket for many sides, and in January 2023 he became the first to reach 100 appearances in the Bangladesh Premier League. He retired from one-day internationals in March 2025.

And finally

A history graduate who spent two decades making some of his own: there are worse ways to use a degree.
